content:
Although I usually prefer using my iPhone without any case or screen protector, for the iPhone 17 Pro I actually applied a screen protector and put on a case, and I sincerely recommend them to everyone. Neither item is expensive, so give them a try—you can always remove them later if you don't like them.

Five years ago, Apple introduced Ceramic Shield glass for the iPhone display, claiming at the time that drop protection performance was improved fourfold, promising to reduce the occurrence of cracked screens.

I myself have never dropped my iPhone and cracked the screen, but after using it for a year, I would often see two or three deep scratches.

This year's Ceramic Shield 2 front cover claims a threefold improvement in scratch resistance.

Apple also says the panel's anti-glare performance has improved, reducing reflections, but the effect still falls far short of the nano-texture found on the iPad Pro and MacBook Pro.

Giving your iPhone 17 Pro screen a more matte finish

For these reasons, I'm using a product I tried a few years ago and quite liked—the matte glass screen protector from Mothca.

This product isn't perfect. If I had a choice, I'd much rather have an iPhone with nano-texture, without having to put up with slight rainbow patterns and reduced brightness.

However, if you're interested in a matte screen for your iPhone, it's still worth a try—especially since a single or two-pack costs just $9 or $14, and the feel is even better than what the price would suggest.

A slim case for emergency use

When it comes to cases, I don't want to spend too much, because I don't plan to use one every day.

I usually put on a case before activities like kayaking or mounting my iPhone on a motorcycle handlebar. I'm also worried that the sharp edges of the camera bump will scratch the orange aluminum frame.

I like black, but I feel that paired with cosmic orange it has a bit of a Halloween vibe—not really suitable for year-round use. In the end, I decided to go with a greyer color, thinking it would create a futuristic spacesuit feel when matched with the orange.

I happened to see this case in a physical store a few days ago, and I've been quite happy with it after using it.

Spigen's Thin Fit comes in three colors: black, gunmetal grey, or abyss green. I chose the grey one, which matched the look I was going for.

Spigen's official site lists it at $39.99, but the same model is only $34.99 on Amazon.

I've noticed that many inexpensive cases don't support MagSafe, which affects the performance of external batteries and magnetic stands when used.

The Spigen Thin Fit includes both MagSafe and a capacitive Camera Control cover, rather than just a cutout.

What I like about this case is that it covers the entire camera 'plateau,' because that's exactly the spot where I'm most concerned about durability.

Once installed, it also creates a really nice 'orange ring' design, looking similar to the digital crown on a space black Apple Watch Ultra.

The cosmic orange accent also appears on the button covers, not just at the bottom port area, creating the orange-and-grey look I was after.

Another benefit is that once installed, you can't see the orange aluminum edge around the screen. That edge actually looks quite nice on its own, but with a dark case and dark screen, a thin strip of orange showing in between can look quite jarring.

Two affordable iPhone 17 Pro accessory recommendations

The Mothca screen protector can help you avoid deep scratches, and if you like anti-glare screens, its matte feel is also excellent. The Spigen Thin Fit case offers a metallic, smooth feel without making the device too bulky.
